title: Dispatch: end-to-end useItem regression coverage for timer re-entry (attempt 2)
description:
Follow-up dispatch for eshyra-jw56. The eshyra-iohn dispatch implemented the fix
correctly (schema marker, timer preservation, engine wiring, curation, pack
regeneration) but did not add the end-to-end coverage its plan called for.
Supervisor diff review found two gaps. This bead closes them. No production code
should change.

Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` for the design decision and the source-backed
curation table.

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`, cut from branch
`eshyra-jw56` (which already carries the eshyra-iohn fix). Work only there.

## Gap 1 — `packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts` has no coverage at all

The bead's actual reported defect goes through `useItem`, and nothing exercises
it. Acceptance criterion 1 of eshyra-jw56 ("repeated `spell-contact-loss` cannot
extend the Cube of Force barrier") is currently unproven end to end: the engine
wiring at `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts` ~1852
(`selectedTransition.nextState === state?.machineState && !resetsDuration`) is
only covered indirectly by unit tests of `resolveItemStateTimers`.

Add a test to `packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts` using the existing fixture
idiom in that file — see the "initializes and plays Flame Tongue toggle state"
test (~line 121) for `item()`, `giveItem`, `createInitialItemState`,
`writeItemState`, `useItem`, `useInput`, `pack()` and the
`db.prepare('UPDATE clock SET elapsed_minutes=? WHERE id=1').run()` idiom.

Build one fixture machine that mirrors the Cube of Force shape and assert all
three arms in the same test (or three focused tests):

1. enter a timed state at minute 0 -> `pendingTimers` deadline is anchored;
2. advance the clock, then fire a self-transition **without** `resetsDuration`
   -> `deadlineElapsedMinutes` and `anchorElapsedMinutes` are unchanged (this is
   the regression: it used to move);
3. advance the clock, then fire a self-transition **with**
   `resetsDuration: true` -> re-anchored to the current clock;
4. a cross-state transition into a different timed state -> fresh anchor.

Assert on the persisted state too (`readItemState`), not only the `useItem`
return value.

## Gap 2 — `packages/core/test/itemTimers.test.ts` non-matching preserved entry

The reworked test "preserves matching timers and leaves unrelated declarations
fresh" only covers the matching case (its `unmatched` variable is in fact a
match on `from`+`to`). Add the genuinely unmatched case: pass a `preserved`
array whose entries do **not** match the declaration's `to`, and assert the
declaration resolves fresh against the clock. Consider renaming the misleading
`unmatched` binding.

## Constraints

- Tests only. If you believe production code must change, stop and report it in
  your completion notes instead of changing it.
- Do not weaken or delete existing assertions (`docs/importer-fix-protocol.md`).
- `npm ci` first (fresh worktree). `npm run verify:worktree` **before**
  committing (it rewrites files). Commit on your branch.
- Do not push, do not open a PR, do not merge. Never modify eshyra-jw56 or
  eshyra-iohn.
notes:
## Gap 3 (added by supervisor at integration) — source-grounding comment

`packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts`
(~line 277) now reads:

    // Source: pressing a different face resets the duration; pressing
    // the already-active face is the explicit reset-duration ruling.

That cites the wrong sentence. The "different face" clause covers the
*cross-face* transitions, which re-anchor automatically because they change
state — it is not the grounding for the marker. The marker's grounding is the
general activation sentence: "You can use an action to press one of the cube's
faces... a barrier of invisible force springs into existence... and lasts for
1 minute", which applies to any face press including the already-active one.

Rewrite that comment to cite the activation sentence. This is the one
production-file edit allowed by this bead; it is comment-only and must not
change generated pack output (confirm with `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`).
